title: Radisys Launches V.AI Ecosystem for Telecom AI Service Innovation - The Fast Mode
content: Radisys, a global leader in open telecom solutions, announced the launch of its V.AI ecosystem, bringing together applications, development tools and leading voice and speech AI technologies to help telecom operators create, deploy and monetize AI-powered communication services for consumers and business subscribers. The V.AI ecosystem, which has evolved since the launch of the Radisys Engage Digital Platform (EDP) at MWC Barcelona in 2022, draws on two decades of Radisys leadership in real-time media processing and a global footprint across live operator networks. Seamlessly integrated with EDP, the ecosystem gives operators multiple paths to market. Operators can deploy turnkey applications, customize services for specific markets and customer segments, or create new device-independent, network-delivered experiences through V.AI Studio, Radisys’ development environment for voice and video AI services. Charter members of the V.AI ecosystem, ElevenLabs, Hiya, ReadSpeaker, Sensory, and Speechmatics expand the range of voice and speech AI capabilities available through EDP. Radisys has combined these technologies with its telecom network, device (mobile and landline handsets, cameras, sensors and more), and media processing capabilities to deliver end-to-end AI-enhanced applications across pre-call, in-call, and post-call experiences. Applications include agentic assistants, intelligent fraud protection, call screening, personalized call clarity, live call translation, intelligent call recording, 5G New Calling, Industry 4.0 automation with video analytics, and more. V.AI ecosystem partners bring specialized AI capabilities, including broad language support, optimized compute efficiency, and industry-leading accuracy, as well as the flexibility to deploy AI services directly within operator networks and/or in public cloud infrastructure. By running Radisys EDP and V.AI partner solutions within their own managed infrastructure, service providers can achieve cost-efficient deployment and automation while meeting their data security, privacy, and sovereignty requirements. This deployment model also minimizes latency and helps meet demanding performance SLAs. Through the V.AI Studio, operators can customize EDP's off-the-shelf application library, with SDKs, a visual application designer, and scripting tools to create new services. Built on a cloud-native telecom platform, EDP enables secure, automated, and scalable services that meet operator requirements and provide reliable experiences for their customers. Support for network APIs (GSMA CAMARA) allows AI-enhanced EDP applications to leverage network assets such as identity, location, and guaranteed quality of service levels that pure over-the-top applications can’t match. The platform also enables advanced 5G New Calling experiences today, while providing a seamless migration path to end-to-end, device-to-network IMS Data Channel support. This delivers immersive, no-app, no-download experiences on mobile devices, simplifying adoption and accelerating service innovation, while natural speech interfaces extend access to the same applications via feature phones and landlines. In addition to the capabilities of Radisys’ V.AI ecosystem, EDP also supports integrations with public cloud-based AI speech technologies, including Azure Speech from Microsoft, Google Cloud Speech-to-Text and Cloud Text-to-Speech APIs, and the OpenAI Audio API for speech transcription and audio translation capabilities.1 2 3 Uniquely in the market, EDP applications can be distributed across the telecom cloud, network edge, and devices, including app-based and app-less experiences enabled through IMS Data Channel, allowing each service to run where it best balances infrastructure cost, performance, data governance and operational requirements. Radisys has enabled AI-driven services through EDP with production deployments across North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. To learn more about Radisys’ Voice and Speech AI applications and the V.AI ecosystem, visit https://www.engagedigital.ai/. Meet Radisys at CASA26, September 21-22 at the Tobacco Theater in Amsterdam to experience V.AI applications and learn how EDP and the V.AI ecosystem can help operators accelerate service innovation and create new sources of customer value and revenue. Al Balasco, Head of Media, Core and Applications Business, Radisys By combining Radisys EDP with the capabilities of our V.AI ecosystem partners, we enable service providers to achieve faster time-to-market, stronger service assurance, and unparalleled ROI,” said Al Balasco, Head of Media, Core and Applications Business, Radisys. “Through this integrated approach, operators benefit from unmatched performance and greater operational and economic value than public cloud-only alternatives, with more control over the capabilities of their applications. Raul Castanon-Martinez, Sr. Analyst, 451 Research from S&P Global The communications platform-as-a-service market is on a trajectory to become a cornerstone of digital engagement. Our 2026 Programmable Communications Market Monitor & Forecast projects it will reach $35.4 billion by 2030. Because over-the-top players capture most of this value, communication service providers risk being relegated to simple connectivity providers. Radisys EDP directly addresses this strategic challenge, enabling CSPs to monetize their network infrastructure investments through application-layer services. This presents a clear path to launching competitive, high-margin digital services, Ray Sharma is an Industry Analyst and Editor at The Fast Mode. He has over 15 years of experience in mobile broadband technologies and solutions, conducting research and analysis on various technology segments and producing articles and write-ups on the latest developments within the sector. He is also in charge of social media engagement and industry liaisons. Follow him on LinkedIn or Facebook. He can be reached at ray.sharma@thefastmode.com

title: Infineon RISC-V for Automotive at Hot Chips 2026 - ServeTheHome
content: Since we covered many of the other talks, we also had a draft of the Infineon RISC-V for Automotive talk for Hot Chips 2026 ready. We figured, why not give this talk some exposure too? Let us get to it. Infineon opened with the compute demands facing automotive microcontrollers. Chassis, powertrain, and ADAS applications together want real-time low latency, power efficiency, and security on top of the highest integrity levels and functional safety, all on a single part. Architecture work starts with the move from domain architecture toward zone control units and eventually full car computers. Former domain controllers evolve into central car computers handling ADAS, infotainment, and vehicle motion, while body and comfort functions consolidate into zones that share wiring and cut harness weight and cost. In automotive, the wiring harness is a huge deal. Infineon lays out the real-time areas that every automotive part must handle. Fast control loops such as E-motor control need deadlines under 10 ms and interrupt latencies in the tens of nanoseconds, while strategic functions like vehicle management tolerate multiple seconds and 10 ms interrupt latency. We heard some of this in the Waymo Sensor Fusion Processor at Hot Chips 2026 talk. With zone architecture in place, the open question is how much intelligence each zone controller should carry. Path A uses optimized multi-domain zone controllers that partially consolidate endpoint ECUs and support local power distribution, while Path B keeps zone controllers as low-complexity I/O aggregators with no intelligence of their own. Infineon says that Option A is the more advantageous path. Keeping local tactics and latency-sensitive control loops in the zone while global strategies and OEM value sit in the central compute shrinks the vehicle attack surface, eases maintenance, and cuts system cost by consolidating endpoint ECUs and decentralizing power distribution. Real zone controllers integrate workloads with very different compute demands. Real-time control, DSP and AI inference, low-power service layers, and audio processing all land on one part, so the compute architecture must scale across high-end multi-domain zones and low-end body zones while still delivering good power, performance, and area. A super-integrated zone controller pushes heterogeneity further by adding an MPU island alongside the MCU. Offloading non-real-time critical workloads to a POSIX adaptive software stack frees the real-time core, enables faster boot and wake than a full SoC, and helps a zone scale from L2 toward L2+ and L3. Against that backdrop, Infineon makes the case for RISC-V, which feels a bit like RISC-V over Arm given many of the other solutions out there. A single open and scalable ISA avoids IP-level lock-in, eases knowledge sharing, and brings ecosystem synergies across automotive, IoT, and industrial use. Standardization depends on the right profiles. Within the RVI AUTO-SIG discussion, Infineon argues the distinction is less about auto versus non-auto and more about defining industry-grade safety- and security-related products, starting from a base such as RV32E and I plus M and U and adding optionalities for supervisor mode, floating point, vectors, and hypervisor support. If you want to learn more about profiles there was an Update on RISC-V Standards and Adoption at Hot Chips 2026. Scalability depends as much on the software stack as on the ISA. Infineon points to virtualization as a key requirement so an RVM-based system can host multiple workloads and software domains cleanly. RISC-V specifies the ISA rather than implementation details. Instruction latency, memory hierarchy, cache coherency, and functional safety features such as lock-step and error tracking stay in the hands of the silicon designer, which is where automotive differentiation happens. Infineon says that in practice, detailed ISA aspects matter less than microarchitectural optimization, and for MCUs the winning attributes are memory, connectivity, specific hardware, sourcing, and final BOM cost, with the availability of automotive-qualified toolchains deciding who succeeds. Infineon closes by tying RISC-V to concrete zone controller roles. RISC-V can accelerate zone control units, but application and cost fit are driven by factors beyond the ISA, such as SoC architecture, ecosystem enablement, and ease of deployment, and long-term adoption depends on standardized hardware-software interfaces and toolchain support. That mix of open ISA freedom and the need for dependable, toolchain-backed automotive silicon frames where RISC-V fits as zone architectures mature. Infineon frames RISC-V as an ISA that removes the lock-in, but the market will be won on auto-qualified toolchains, SoC architecture, and ecosystem enablement rather than the instruction set alone. Hopefully, the automotive folks are able to support multiple ISAs unless one clearly pulls ahead. title: Instant analysis of Jaguars Week 1 win v. Browns - Yahoo Sports
content: The Jacksonville Jaguars are 1-0 after cruising to victory in the season opener against the Cleveland Browns. With the clock at zero, here are our instant takeaways from their performance. - In a game that you're expected to win, the Jaguars did exactly what they're supposed to do -- control the matchup from start to finish. - Trevor Lawrence had an excellent day, completing 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards with four touchdown passes. - The Jaguars' run game was very efficient. Led by Bhayshul Tuten and Ameer Abdullah, the Jaguars averaged nearly 5.0 yards per rush as a team. - Parker Washington picked up where he left off last season. - Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr. also added five receptions for 80 yards between the two of them. - As expected, we saw both Ventrell Miller and Branson Combs at linebacker. Miller led the team in total tackles by a wide margin. - The Jaguars did well to get after Deshaun Watson, totaling five sacks. Cleveland playing from behind for much of the game helped create obvious passing situations for the Jaguars' front to exploit. - No surprise here, but Cam Little was perfect on field goals and extra points. - The Jaguars' offense was efficient on third downs. The defense was also very good in those situations against the Browns. The Jaguars were good in the red zone as well. title: Man United v Man City player ratings from highly controversial Manchester derby - Yahoo Sports
content: Erling Haaland's controversial goal earned 10-man Manchester City a famous victory over Manchester United in the Premier League at Old Trafford. The visitors played down to 10 men for well over an hour after Phil Foden kicked out at United captain Bruno Fernandes, who had punted him in the back first. United were then twice denied by the frame of the goal as the played against the 10-man visitors, with Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo striking the post with shots from distance. Haaland struck on the hour-mark but United will be furious that it was allowed to stand as Enzo Fernandez appeared to be interfering with play from an offside position. However, United struggled to break down the 10-man City, although goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma produced a huge save in stoppage time to deny Bryan Mbeumo. Senne Lammens, 5: Manchester City had one big chance and scored it, with Haaland beating the goalkeeper at the back post. Diogo Dalot, 4: Wasteful when Bruno Fernandes carved the City defence open with a pass over the top. Guilty of lapses at the back. Harry Maguire, 5: An improved showing from his early season form but struggled in possession in the second half. Lisandro Martinez, 5: Lost Haaland at the back post, although he has an argument that Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play from an offside position. Patrick Dorgu, 4: Enjoyed some brighter moments early on but was caught out defensively at times in the second half. Kobbie Mainoo, 5: Unlucky with an effort from range that hit the post but United needed more when they were playing against 10 men. Youri Tielemans, 5: A strange decision from Michael Carrick to take off the midfielder. United quickly ran out of ideas. Bryan Mbeumo, 3: Simply had to score when Bruno Fernandes found him in the box in stoppage time. Wasteful. Bruno Fernandes, 5: Well below his best and fortunate he wasn't punished for kicking Phil Foden in the contentious first-half sending off. Marcus Rashford, 6: Bright and buzzy from the left wing. Unlucky with a free-kick that had Donnarumma beaten but struck the post. United's best player on the day. Matheus Cunha, 3: Like his other forwards, struggled to provide end product and looked lost up front. Benjamin Sesko, 5: There's an argument he should have been brought on earlier but he also struggled to make an impact against City's defence. Gianluigi Donnarumma, 9: An astonishing save to deny Mbeumo from point-blank range at the death. Matheus Nunes, 8: Arguably City's best player in the first half. Excellent in his battle against Rashford. Marc Guehi, 9: A superb showing from the England defender in the second half as the 10 men of City held on. Ruben Dias, 8: Didn't put a foot wrong next to Guehi in defence. They earned their clean sheet. Josko Gvardiol, 8: The left back picked his moment to get forward to perfection as he found Haaland at the back post. Elliot Anderson, 9: A stunning first derby form City's new midfielder. Grew in stature as the game went on with timely tackles. Enzo Fernandez, 8: How City benefited from having his character in the derby. Rightly taken off before he could have boiled over, though. Phil Foden, 1: Oh dear. There's clearly an argument that Fernandes got away with one, but that's no excuse for what Foden did. Rayan Cherki, 4: Took an early knock when Harry Maguire clattered into him but his little flashes of magic disappeared after City were reduced to 10 men. Replaced at half-time. Antoine Semenyo, 6: A bit sloppy in possession at times and struggled in the final third but worked hard for his side after going down to 10 men. Erling Haaland, 8: He only needed one chance – and it was a half chance at that. Simply immense for City. Iliman Ndiaye: 8: A superb substitution at half-time from Enzo Maresca. Carried and looked after the ball extremely well.

title: Phil Foden sees red but Erling Haaland scores winner - Manchester Utd v City player ratings - bbc.com
content: Manchester City's Phil Foden reacts after being sent off against Manchester United at Old Trafford Phil Foden's first-half red card did not prevent Manchester City extending their perfect start to the season by beating Manchester United at Old Trafford. Here's how Simon Stone rated the United players and Shamoon Hafez scored City's. Senne Lammens: Not as busy as he might have expected to be. Absolutely vital save from Fernandez to prevent City second. 7 Diogo Dalot: If only he had been able to control Bruno Fernandes' chipped pass into the penalty area he might have marked his 250th Manchester United appearance with a rare goal. Didn't look down the line to see he was clearly offside as United pressed just before half-time. Screwed shot wide after break. 4 Harry Maguire: Decent performance from veteran central defender and not far away from an equaliser with late header. Needless push on Enzo Fernandez in the box, for which he was booked. 6 Lisandro Martinez: Didn't dive in when Bruno Fernandes played a pass towards his own goal straight to Erling Haaland and won the ball from the Norwegian. Decent effort 7 Patrick Dorgu: Replaced Luke Shaw at left back in the starting 11 and did OK but doesn't have the same link with Rashford. Attempted block proved so crucial to City's opener. 6 Kobbie Mainoo: Another assured display in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel. Came close to giving his side the lead just after half-time and was home side's most effective midfielder. 8 Youri Tielemans (off 66, Sesko): Best performance of the season so far but yet to make the standout contribution expected. 7 Bryan Mbeumo: Probably United's most-effective attacking player. Header just wide before injury-time effort saved. 8 Bruno Fernandes: Fortunate to get away with no sanction at all over the incident that led to Foden's dismissal. Not one of his better efforts 6 Marcus Rashford (off 83, Zirkzee): Curling long-range free-kick against the post with Donnarumma beaten and shot into side-netting but still waiting for first goal since his return. 6 Matheus Cunha: Preferred to Benjamin Sesko in starting line-up and dragged early shot wide. Got involved on plenty of occasions, but again by dropping deep. Off target with a second-half opportunity. 7 Benjamin Sesko (on 66, Tielemans): Brought on to make an impact and tried his luck from distance soon afterwards. 6 Subs not used: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Lacey. Gianluigi Donnarumma: Saw his post hit twice but made a good stop to deny Fernandes from range and a sensational one in injury-time from Mbeumo for the clean sheet. 8 Matheus Nunes: Overcome his nightmare performance here from April 2025. Showed some neat touches and generally shackled Rashford well. 7 Ruben Dias: The Portuguese has stepped up to take on the responsibility of being captain and was solid at the back once again. 7 Marc Guehi: Beginning to form an impressive partnership with his skipper and needed to be sturdy after City were reduced to 10 men. 7 Josko Gvardiol: Looks like left-back is where his position will be in this team. Handled Mbeumo brilliantly throughout and provided the cross for Haaland's goal. 8 Elliot Anderson: Busy and hard working in the centre of the park, as is now expected. Managed more touches of the ball than any City team-mate. 7 Enzo Fernandez: Given licence to roam and has fitted in seamlessly into midfield. The Argentine made an excellent challenge to thwart Tielemans and struck the post in the second half. 8 Antoine Semenyo: Has struggled in recent games and was wasteful once more. Place in the starting XI could come under pressure from Iliman Ndiaye. 5 Phil Foden: Total head loss in the cauldron of the derby. Given a straight red after kicking Fernandes in the stomach on 23 minutes and fortunate not to cost his side. 3 Rayan Cherki: Created very little after being move to the right. Not helped by a fellow attacking player getting himself sent off before being taken off at half-time. 5 Erling Haaland: On the periphery of the game in the first half, the fewest touches of any player. But came alive to open the scoring in with a cool, first-time finish in front of his own fans. 7 Iliman Ndiaye (on 45, Cherki): Caused some concern to the United backline with his direct running. 6 Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Reis, Bouaddi, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis. title: Breaking down the falsehoods behind Dominion v. Fox and voting in America - Texas Public Radio | TPR
content: In the aftermath of the 2020 presidential election, Fox News repeatedly broadcast claims that Dominion Voting Systems had helped steal the election from President Donald Trump. Those allegations were false, but their consequences produced one of the most significant media-law cases in American history. In “Terrible Stuff Damaging Everybody: The True Story of Lies and Libel in Dominion v. Fox,” media attorney Ian Rosenberg reconstructs the lawsuit from thousands of pages of court filings, internal communications and sworn testimony. The title comes from a message Fox Corporation Chairman Rupert Murdoch sent as Trump attorney Rudy Giuliani promoted election-fraud allegations: “Terrible stuff damaging everybody, I fear.” Rosenberg portrays the case as a three-act drama: why Fox aired the accusations, what the litigation exposed about the company’s internal decision-making, and what the outcome could mean for journalism and defamation law. Dominion sought $1.6 billion, arguing that Fox hosts and guests promoted unsupported accusations involving manipulated software and switched votes. Fox maintained that it was covering newsworthy allegations made by the president’s lawyers and defended its reporting under the First Amendment. But internal messages revealed that some Fox hosts, producers and executives privately doubted or rejected claims being presented to viewers. In March 2023, Delaware Superior Court Judge Eric Davis ruled that it was “crystal clear” the challenged statements about Dominion were false. A jury was still expected to determine whether Fox acted with “actual malice”—meaning it knowingly broadcast false information or recklessly disregarded the truth. The trial never began. Fox and Dominion reached a $787.5 million settlement just before opening statements. Fox acknowledged the court’s findings but did not apologize or admit liability. Fox said the agreement reflected its commitment to journalistic standards. Rosenberg argues that the case ultimately demonstrates both sides of American libel law: strong protections allow journalists to make honest mistakes, but those protections do not provide immunity for knowingly or recklessly spreading falsehoods. His book presents the litigation as a warning about what can happen when audience loyalty, political pressure and commercial interests overtake basic verification. Ian Rosenberg is a media lawyer with over 25 years of experience specializing in First Amendment, libel and news law. He is also an Adjunct Associate Professor at Brooklyn College. Previously Rosenberg was an Assistant Chief Counsel advising ABC News, and an Emmy-nominated documentary filmmaker. He is the author of “TerribleStuff Damaging Everybody: The True Story of Lies and Libel inDominion v. title: Pollock: Bills v Texans Prediction - the wellsville sun
content: Joe Brady will get a major test in his first game as Bills head coach. Buffalo’s former offensive coordinator replaces the fired Sean McDermott for this afternoon’s game at Houston’s NRG Stadium (1 o’clock, CBS-TV, Bills Radio Network). Brady’s offense will be charged with facing the defending No. 1 NFL defense. He’ll be on the sideline calling offensive plays while defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard will be in the same place doing a similar chore for his unit. Buffalo’s offensive advantage is former NFL MVP Josh Allen at quarterback paired with league defending rushing champion, RB James Cook. They figure to get a lift from former Panther and Bear, D.J. Moore at wideout. The Bills’ problem is defense where the lack of depth renders it a decidedly pedestrian unit even though Buffalo is favored by 1 1/2 points. For the Texans, pass-rush specialist Will Anderson has missed the last two practices before participating in Saturday’s walk-through and he’s supposedly healthy. WHEN ASKED about his first game as an NFL head coach, Brady allowed he hasn’t contemplated the consequences. “I’ve got enough on my plate game-planning and trying to lead a football team. It’ll never be about me.” He added, “All I care about is doing what the heck we have to do to go 1-0. It’s so cliche and coachspeak … but it’s who we are. It doesn’t have to look good, it doesn’t have to be pretty. “Just put the ball down and play the next one and do what we have to do to get one more point than them.” (Chuck Pollock, a Wellsville Sun and Olean Star senior sports columnist, can be reached at cpollock@wnynet.net.) title: Premier League schedule today: How to watch, TV channels & live stream - theguardian.com
content: How will Manchester United and Manchester City fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options The first Manchester Derby of the season comes at an interesting time for both clubs. City are building momentum under new manager Enzo Maresca while United are attempting to move on from a summer that raised questions about their transfer market strategy. After conceding two goals in each of their three league games so far, Manchester United have made their worst defensive start to a season since 1972. Meanwhile, Manchester City would win their opening four Premier League games for a record seventh time with victory at Old Trafford. United got the better of City in last season’s league meeting at the Theatre of Dreams. A lot has changed since then, but the Manchester Derby is always one of English soccer’s fiercest fixtures. Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s Premier League fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks, and online streaming options. Michael Carrick insists Manchester United’s current outlook “is not that bad” despite the Old Trafford outfit winning just one of their first three league fixtures to start the season. Defeat in Sunday’s derby would make it harder for the United manager to deny the growing malaise around the club. The failure to land a single new non-midfielder in the summer transfer window left some supporters with the sense Manchester United could have done more to prepare for the season ahead. Nonetheless, Carrick possesses the attacking quality to win any game. Maresca boasts the same. Erling Haaland already has five goals to his name this season. Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez are bedding in after blockbuster transfers. Rayan Cherki is growing in influence with almost every match he plays. Pep Guardiola might be gone, but Manchester City still have a fear factor. Player to watch: Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United - If the hosts are to get the better of their rivals on Sunday, their best player will surely have to play a key role. Last season’s Premier League Player of the Season is a creative force of nature. Fernandes has the capacity to win the derby on his own.

title: Diablo V: Forging the Next Era - Blizzard News
content:
Igniting our celebration of 30 years, we unveiled the Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel at BlizzCon 2026. The development team revealed the first details of the world, classes, and systems taking shape in Diablo V. You’ll become the Heir to Westmarch and traverse a Sanctuary actively reshaped by Diablo, accompanied by a growing caravan of survivors. The team also unveiled the Demon Hunter, Monk, and all-new Plague Knight classes and shared how past Diablo games are inspiring a renewed focus on item depth, clarity, and identity. These early ideas all flow from the central premise at the heart of Diablo V: the heroes of the past have failed, Sanctuary has fallen, and Diablo has won. This is the foundation for Diablo’s next era, and only the beginning of what the team plans to share as development continues. Catch up on the full Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel here: Diablo has conquered Sanctuary, a stepping stone to invading the Heavens. Now from the throne of Westmarch, he wields Sanctuary's people and souls as weapons in the Eternal Conflict. Diablo is no longer a distant threat waiting at the end of the journey. He is present from the moment Diablo V begins, shaping the story, the world, and your path through it. As Heir to Westmarch, on the run through the charred remains of a kingdom now transformed into an outpost of Hell. Few humans have escaped Diablo’s rule. Some have bowed before him or joined his cults, while a terrifying few have been corrupted into Dread Commanders and raised to rival the powers of Hell. Your mysterious connection to Diablo makes you both a threat and uniquely vulnerable to his powerful influence. With Sanctuary’s greatest champions gone, what must you become to fight for the home taken from you? This is not Sanctuary waiting for the apocalypse. It is already living through one. In Diablo V, humanity has fallen into ruin, and the Western Continent is at the heart of Diablo’s reign of terror. We revealed a haunting, desolate land shaped by despair, resilience, and the few survivors fighting to endure another day. Sanctuary itself is no longer stable. Diablo is actively reshaping the world through terror, reflected by a procedural landscape where terrain, points of interest, monsters, and reward can change when you return. It’s ruins tell the story of what was lost, its corruption reveals Diablo’s present rule, and the encroaching forces of Hell offer a glimpse of what comes next. With Sanctuary under Diablo’s rule, survival is no longer tied to towns or conquered strongholds. Instead, you’ll need to build a caravan of allies who travel with you through the scorched wastes. These allies will be both vendors and steadfast companions, a growing community full of stories to discover. They are fascinating characters with pasts, stakes, and scars from surviving in Diablo’s Sanctuary. Amongst your newfound companions are a former Sister of the Sightless Eye... and a stranded Treasure Goblin searching for meaning in a world where greed has lost its purpose. The team offered an early look at how they’re thinking about class identity, progression, and loot. During the panel, we revealed the first three classes coming to Diablo V: The Demon Hunter returns to stalk the forces of Hell with twin crossbows, striking from the shadows and leaping across the battlefield to annihilate their prey. The Monk brings martial perfection back to Sanctuary, battering demons to a pulp with fists and calling down holy power to smite those who stand in their path. The all-new Plague Knight is the embodiment of walking death. They roam the battlefield, spreading disease and pestilence, ultimately consuming it for power. These are only the first of the classes we’ll reveal on the road to Diablo V, with more details on their combat, progression, and build possibilities to come. The team emphasized their goal is to design items to feel readable, memorable, and worth chasing across hundreds of hours. Itemization in Diablo V is inspired by Diablo II. We’re experimenting with stat requirements on gear. Your inventory plays a key role in how you wield your arsenal, larger items once again take up more slots in your inventory. Gear-based sets are also returning for Diablo V. This will be a rich and deep crafting system, inspired by Lord of Hatred’s approach, with Diablo II-style Runes and Runewords. Diablo V is still early in development, and this reveal marks the beginning of an ongoing conversation with the Diablo player community. Starting in 2027, we plan to share regular updates offering a closer look at our progress, the ideas guiding development, and features taking shape along the way. Bringing players into the process early gives us the opportunity to listen, understand what excites you the most, and allow that to inform the decisions ahead. We want to build a Diablo game that honors what players love while taking the series somewhere genuinely new. The next era has only begun. Sign up for future updates at Diablo5.Blizzard.com. title: Diablo V First Look: Blizzard’s Next Sequel Doubles Down on Darkness - Esquire
content: Only three years after Diablo IV, Blizzard reveals the next sequel of its hit RPG series exclusively to Esquire. The end is now. Three and a half years after Diablo IV, Blizzard Entertainment is announcing the next installment in its popular action role-playing series: Diablo V. For the first time in more than 15 years, players will square off with the Big D himself, Diablo, who has changed quite a bit since he rose as the ultimate Prime Evil. Diablo V is scheduled to launch in 2029 on platforms Blizzard has yet to announce. “You’re entering Diablo V with Sanctuary in an apocalypse,” says Joe Shely, senior game director, in an exclusive interview with Esquire. “Sanctuary is not a happy place in the best of times, but Diablo V takes it to another level. You’re living in a world that has been overrun by Diablo. He sits on the throne, humanity is destroyed, and players themselves are on the run.” “You’ve spent the last 30 years fending off the apocalypse,” adds Jennifer Hepler, narrative director of Diablo V. “We were like, What if Diablo won and we scramble to claw back territory by our fingernails? We wanted to make a world that’s darker than ever but give you a reason to fight for it.” Ahead of the game’s reveal at BlizzCon in Anaheim, California, Esquire sat down with members of the game’s senior development team, who peeled back the curtain on players’ next adventure across Sanctuary as it has fallen under Diablo’s occupation. Next to Shely and Hepler is John Mueller, Diablo V’s senior art director. Together they tell Esquire that the driving question behind the new project was “Wouldn’t it be cool if…?” Wouldn’t it be cool if … we brought back fan-favorite classes? Wouldn’t it be cool if … there was a single memorable space full of interesting people? Wouldn’t it be cool if … the story was centered entirely on the players’ characters? These questions drove Blizzard to pursue a full-fledged entry in the mainline series. Usually a new game coming a few years after the previous installment isn’t so earth-shattering for a hit video game series. But Diablo is not an ordinary series. Since Diablo II was released in 2000, fans have spent literal decades waiting for just a glimpse of sequels like Diablo III (released in 2012) and Diablo IV (released in 2023). Waiting out epochs is routine for fans. But all their waiting and wondering for what’s next ends now. What’s next is a heated reunion with Diablo. Esquire has the first-ever exclusive look at Diablo V with its concept art below. “We wanted to turn back to the title villain, who we haven’t seen in over ten years, since Diablo III,” says Shely. “He needs his own game. There are things we can do, in terms of innovations and how we tell the story, that give us a fresh slate.” Set a century after Diablo IV, Diablo V casts players as the runaway heir to the lost kingdom of Westmarch. They share a mysterious connection with Diablo, who has since evolved from a big, bad guy of fire and brimstone into a more calculated antagonist. “We wanted to give players a lot of agency in the story,” explains Hepler, the main architect of Diablo V’s story. In contrast to how players spend time in Diablo IV forging connections with Lilith and Mephisto, Hepler says they wanted players to feel their bonds “much faster” in Diablo V. “The story starts when you find you’re the only one who can go into Diablo’s terror realm and come back alive,” she says. “We wanted to give you that core identity we could build the story around. You’re not a wanderer in someone else’s story.” Hepler adds: “In past games, Diablo was brutish. What did Diablo learn from watching Mephisto? Diablo has learned how to be subtle. He is the Lord of Terror; what does terror mean? What does someone whose entire existence is provoking or feeding on fear going to be like? We want to give you that bond with him from the beginning. Why is Diablo interested in you? How you define yourself in the shadow of, and in opposition to, Diablo is a big part of the game. He is trying to control you. What do you do to push back?” Hepler clarifies that players still retain plenty of individual customization over their characters, like in their character classes. “You aren’t a fixed character. This is not Nathan Drake. This is still an ARPG. The Heir to Westmarch in your world is whatever gender and class you pick.” “You’ll shape who you are as a character, as the heir, more freely than you ever have before,” adds Joe Shely. “The idea of who you are as a person and what class you’re playing are independent in a way they’ve never been before. You can look and be whoever you want.” Speaking of classes, Shely says Diablo V “will launch with more classes than we ever had in a Diablo game before.” While the team cannot unpack each class in detail yet, it is revealing three in particular: the returning Monk and Demon Hunter, as well as the new Plague Knight. “The Monk and Demon Hunter are really established fantasies for us,” says John Mueller, who oversees the art direction of Diablo V. “The last time players saw these was Diablo III. In 2012, technology was different. We have advanced through Diablo IV, so we want to give people the best versions of these in 2029.” Shely lays out the Demon Hunter’s and Monk’s individual vibes, in case you weren’t around for Diablo III. “A Demon Hunter has light armor and twin crossbows. They’re extremely agile, pinning demons against walls. It’s a fantasy players are familiar with. And Monk, you know, who doesn’t like pulverizing demons with their fist? It’s an up-close melee class.” Then there’s the Plague Knight, a new control-based character built like a tank that spreads disease. “This is a heavily armored, ‘walking death’ character who will spread disease across the battlefield and consume that disease for power.” Artistically, the team designed the Plague Knight like a medieval iron maiden on two legs. As in any action RPG, players start the game with almost nothing. Over time, they meet new allies who join their nomadic caravan as it roves through a desolate Sanctuary. Blizzard says the caravan serves as the players’ main hub—the only “safe space” in a hellish world—and that it will physically evolve as players progress through the story. “We need there to be something you love about this world,” says Hepler. “Gathering survivors is one of the mechanisms of the story. We’re going through lands where almost everybody is dead or surrendered to Diablo. Now and then we meet a person who has held out, and they become part of the caravan. Your vendors, your craftspeople, everyone who is part of your journey are survivors. These are the people you’re fighting to protect and the source of all your side content.” Hepler reveals that the caravan will change over time as players find new survivors and level up. “Each wagon reflects their personality and background. The wagons upgrade as you go on, reflecting things you’ve done in the story. Trophies from victories appear at the campsite. It becomes a really dynamic place that tracks you in the game.” Adds Mueller, “You start this ragtag [operation]. It’s a shoddy situation. By the end, you’ve grown that into a very aspirational space you love going back to. We think that’s going to be a fun, dynamic way to experience the story.” If Diablo sounds darker than it’s ever been before, which says a lot for a series that’s long epitomized grim-dark video games, that’s by design. Blizzard intends Diablo V to feel bleak and hopeless, which can make every win shine brighter. “We’re doubling down on the darkness,” says Mueller. “Evil has infected everything. Civilization is devastated. The architecture is devastated. Even time has ravaged what’s been left behind. You have this apocalyptic vision of Sanctuary, and for a medieval dark fantasy, it is really compelling.” To that end, Diablo V is returning the franchise to a procedural dungeon system that’s been leveled up with modern software. There is a hundred years’ worth of horror that happened, which players will learn from the environment. “People will want to know what happened in the last hundred years as you’re exploring,” reveals Mueller. “The world is procedural; this is our third generation of procedural dungeon tech. People will get everything they got from the open world of Diablo IV in a dynamic way. You see stories of the past. Stories of survival and tragedy. This is where art is collaborating with narrative closer than ever.” Shely says that the world generation occurs as players move their caravan through the fog of war, like a rickety wagon in a frontier western epic. “The caravan itself moves through the world. It’s not a town that exists in a space. You’re taking your ‘town’ with you through this dangerous place that’s been transformed by the Dread Commanders. You explore, go through the world, and then return to that area with your caravan, and it’s been totally transformed.” While players might think work on Diablo V has just begun, it’s actually been in development for years. There is still more to learn about the game. It won’t release until 2029, which affords anyone still playing through Diablo IV more time to enjoy new, forthcoming content (like Season of Hell’s Legacy, which launches on September 15 to mark the series’ 30th anniversary). When Diablo V eventually arrives, it’ll be about two years into the next console generation. When Esquire asks how Blizzard is developing Diablo V on upcoming platforms, the team keeps mum. “Generally speaking, Blizzard wants to bring our games to as many players as possible,” says Shely, “and so we seek to make Diablo available on many platforms. You can see that with Diablo IV. You should expect the same with Diablo V. We want everyone to take on the Lord of Terror.” For now, all fans should know is that Diablo V is real, and it’s happening sooner than they might have assumed. And waiting for all of them on the long road ahead is one more fight with Diablo. title: BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony: Starcraft Returns, Diablo V Announced, Warcraft news and more - news.xbox.com
content: I’ve been at Blizzard a long time, and I’ve got a bunch of BlizzCons under my belt. Do you know how hard all these announcements were to hold in as we prepared for BlizzCon 2026? I can’t even believe this is real, man, like…okay, sorry, I’m locked in. Whether you’re watching it all unfold live or just catching up later, here is everything from the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony and where to go next for each one. From the farthest reaches of the stars, a new mission calls. StarCraft returns in 2030 as an original open-world shooter. There is really only one thing to say to that, and we said it from the stage and the halls in Anaheim, California: it’s about damn time. Diablo V is coming in Spring 2029, and it opens somewhere the series has never let us stand: after the loss. Sanctuary has fallen. Diablo has won. The question the game asks is what we become when the world we knew is gone. Closer to now, Diablo IV‘s Season of Hell’s Legacy lands September 15 (that’s this Tuesday!) to mark 30 years of Diablo. It brings back the Prime Evils, the Lord of Terror included, along with Deckard Cain, Nightmare Rifts, anniversary rewards, and gear pulled from every era of the series. A little further out, the Amazon joins as the next Diablo IV class in the first half of 2027, javelin in hand. And if you are at the show or playing from home, Moophisto has returned to terrorize the unsuspecting. He is as udderly malevolent as you remember. Heh. XBOX players can save 75% off Diablo IV and up to 30% on Diablo II: Resurrected content now through September 22nd. Everything coming to Sanctuary is on the Diablo website. Ten years of Overwatch, and the team spent its anniversary talking about what comes next. Season 5’s new Support Hero is Doctrine, a life-draining, vampire-inspired healer who sends out bat-like drones. You can play him at BlizzCon right now, and from home for a limited time. He arrives alongside major reworks for Sombra and Roadhog, plus a new map, Watchpoint: Grimsvotn. Season 5 also closes out The Reign of Talon, the first year-long story arc in Overwatch history, and it does not end quietly. The next Overwatch Spotlight follows in February 2027 with the team’s plans for the year. Two things worth clearing your weekend for: YOASOBI plays BlizzCon’s first-ever halftime show during the Overwatch World Cup, and LE SSERAFIM returns to the Main Stage as the closing act, with a new in-game collaboration live now. Then there is QuestWatch, a live Overwatch tabletop RPG one-shot written by Matt Mercer and the Overwatch Narrative team. For those playing on XBOX while you’re streaming at home: play one match to earn a Mythic Voucher and choose an eligible Mythic Hero Skin! More detail on all of it lives on the Overwatch website. Warcraft Goes Backward and Forward at the Same Time We are at the midpoint of The Worldsoul Saga. World of Warcraft‘s next major update, Eclipse (12.2), has Xal’atath closing in on Azeroth’s Worldsoul, and where that goes is up to us. We also got a look at The Last Titan, the final chapter of the Saga, which brings more than two decades of Warcraft storytelling to a close and sets up whatever comes after. More on that early next year. Then a genuine surprise: for the first time in over 23 years, there is a new Warcraft III: Reforged story. The Forsaken Kingdom campaign takes you back to the fall of Lordaeron and its turn into the Undercity, and it ships with the 3.0 update, which brings a substantial graphics overhaul and a revamped World Editor. It is playable today. We dropped it like a Beyonce album. Warcraft III: Reforged is available with XBOX Game Pass, so you only need to pick up the DLC to jump into the new campaign And then we went home. World of Warcraft: Forever is a third way to play alongside Modern and Classic, set in the Vanilla era, with room to explore corners of Azeroth we never got to see the first time: three new zones, over 1,000 new quests, nine new dungeons, two new raids, and the new Skyborne race. It launches November 4, 2026, with Beta starting September 17. The full Warcraft rundown is on the Warcraft website. Hearthstone Opens a Journal and Meets the Old Gods The overhauled Journal pulls every quest, achievement, and event into one place, tied together by the story of each expansion. It keeps a record of where you have been and grows as you keep playing. Reign of the Black Empire hits the Tavern October 20 and takes Hearthstone to the earliest age of Azeroth, long before the Old Gods were imprisoned. Its new keyword, Assemble, merges two cards into a stronger one, which is going to produce some combinations nobody planned for. Before that, on September 22, Battlegrounds adds a new minion type called Aberrations, grown out of Old God corruption and experimentation. Looking further out, the Monk arrives in March 2027 as the game’s first new playable class in six years, fluid and adaptable in the way the class has always been. Xal’atath joins Heroes of the Storm on September 28, playable on the PTR starting September 14. This one belongs to those of you who never stopped playing. There may even be another hero ahead? What year is this? An animated series set in the world of Diablo is in development with Netflix. More on that later, and it is not the only thing taking shape. The BlizzCon livestream runs all weekend with deep dives, panels, and a halftime show, and the full schedule is on the BlizzCon site so you can plan what you want to watch. If you only take three dates with you: Diablo IV‘s Season of Hell’s Legacy launches on September 15, World of Warcraft: Forever Beta opens September 17, and Forever itself launches November 4.  Dude, we’re so back.

title: Diablo V Is Coming Out In Spring 2029 - Engadget
content: Blizzard also confirmed that a Diablo animated series is in development with Netflix. BlizzCon has brought some unexpected news for the Diablo franchise, including a spring 2029 release window for the next installment in the video game series, as well as a confirmation of an animated TV series adaptation in the works with Netflix. For the game, Blizzard's teaser video and article only hints at the story's continuation after the events of Diablo IV, but it looks like players will be thrown straight into hellfire. Like the Diablo V teaser, the confirmation for the animated TV show was equally light on details and we still don't know the release date or which animation studio is in charge of the adaptation. Blizzard said it will have more to share about the series throughout the development process and only hinted that "Sanctuary's darkness is spreading." For those who aren't devoted Diablo fans, rumors of a TV adaptation for the franchise have been circulating for a while. A report from 2020 hinted that a Diablo TV series would be done in an anime style and was in preproduction with Netflix in charge of distribution. Beyond the confirmation of the fifth major game in the franchise and a TV series, Blizzard also hinted at similar adaptations for its other popular titles, including Overwatch and Warcraft.

title: Diablo’s Next Era Revealed at BlizzCon 2026: Opening Ceremonies Recap — Diablo IV - Blizzard News
content:
Thirty years in, Diablo has never had more content ahead of it than now. During the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony, we offered the first glimpse of Diablo V (coming Spring 2029), announced a new animated series set in the world of Diablo in development with Netflix, revealed the Amazon class pack coming to Diablo IV in 2027, unveiled Season of Hell’s Legacy, and confirmed that Diablo IV is coming to Nintendo Switch™ 2. And we’re just getting started. The celebration continues throughout BlizzCon with developer panels, live gameplay, and more from across the franchise, including Diablo Immortal x Spawn. To rewatch BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremonies, you can watch our panel here: Celebrate 30 Years with the Season of Hell’s Legacy Diablo V is officially in development and coming Spring 2029. For the first time, players will enter a Sanctuary where Diablo has triumphed and its heroes have been defeated. At the heart of Diablo V lies a defining question: what must you become when the world has already fallen? Join us for Diablo V: Forging the Next Era panel on September 12, 1:45 p.m. PT for an early look at the world, classes and creative vision shaping the chapter of Diablo. You can also sign up for future updates at Diablo5.Blizzard.com. Sanctuary’s darkness is spreading. Blizzard and Netflix are developing a new animated series set in the world of Diablo, bringing the franchise to a new screen. We’ll have more to share as the series takes shape. Until then, stay awhile... and stay tuned. The Amazon is coming to Diablo IV in the first half of 2027. She hails from the island of Skovos, revealed for the first time in Diablo IV in Lord of Hatred. Her return preserves the disciplined, athletic, and highly trained warrior fantasy players remember while reimagining the class for Diablo IV. Across four gameplay archetypes—Champion, Skirmisher, Ranger, and Commander—the Amazon can wield the returning bow and javelin, which introduces an entirely new weapon type to Diablo IV. Get a closer look at the Amazon in the Diablo IV: What's Next panel on September 13, 11:00 a.m. PT. Additional class pack details will be shared at a later date. More than 130 million players worldwide have entered Sanctuary across the Diablo franchise. Now, three decades of darkness return in Season of Hell’s Legacy, a playable tribute to Diablo’s most iconic characters, foes, locations and loot. In Season of Hell's Legacy, the lost soul of Deckard Cain returns to guide you through an epic journey to redeem the dark wanderers from the torment of the Prime Evils. Confront the Prime Evils Baal, Mephisto, and Diablo, reclaim splinters of their souls, and bear the burden of one of the Splinters to assume a portion of their power. But remember: no demonic gift is bestowed without a steep price. Read more of the legacy the Burning Hells has wrought in our Season Overview blog here, and join us for the Diablo IV: What's Next panel on September 13, 11:00 a.m. PT. Hell has arrived on Nintendo Switch™ 2. The Diablo IV: Age of Hatred Collection is coming to Nintendo Switch™ 2 on September 15. The Diablo IV: Age of Hatred Collection bundles the base game, Vessel of Hatred expansion, and Lord of Hatred expansion. Plunder through the jungles of Nahantu and the far-reaching shores of Skovos to challenge the Lord of Hatred’s hold over Sanctuary on Nintendo Switch™ 2. Note: Nintendo Switch™ 2 supports mouse and keyboard functionality when plugged in via USB, Joy-Con™ 2 mouse functionality is not supported. The 30th anniversary celebration continues throughout BlizzCon weekend with panel highlighting the voice talent behind some of Diablo’s iconic characters and the making of Diablo IV’s cinematics. title: Doris V. Lynch Obituary Sep 12, 2026 - Newcomer Toledo
content:
A clean, simple format with the essential elements. A full-featured format with photos, services, and more. Copy the text below and then paste that into your favorite email application Doris V. Lynch age 93 passed away peacefully on September 12, 2026, surrounded by her family and loved ones. Doris was a lifelong resident of Toledo, Ohio. Born to Raymond and Edna (Merry) Stewart in 1933, Doris was the fourth child of this union and the only girl. She loved climbing trees, peddling papers, playing baseball with her brothers, and sneaking to watch movies at the Avalon theater. Her first movie was Gone with the Wind. Doris leaves behind a beautiful living legacy: four generations of a family that knows how to love, support, and cherish one another because she showed us the way. Doris was known by many names, but her favorite was Nana. She was a grandmother to 17, a great-grandma to 22, and a great-great-grandma to 3. Over the years she cared for and welcomed a number of children into her home and into her life and counted them as bonus grandchildren. It did not matter who you were or your age, Doris would welcome you into her home as family and make sure you didn’t leave hungry. Before you would leave, she would point at you and say, “don’t take any wooden nickels”. Doris and her husband, Larry, were active in the Sheriff’s Auxiliary and the Glass City CB Club, her CB handle was “Ding Dong” because she was also the local Avon lady. She sold Avon for over fifty-years making many connections and new friends along the way. Doris was a volunteer at heart, taking children home from the St. Anthony’s Villa for respite, helping with her daughter’s Girl Scout troops, and in her later years sitting on the board of Neighborhood Housing as Secretary. Doris had many hobbies including collecting Shirley Temple memorabilia, watching Little House on the Prairie, and her love of genealogy, creating binders of the family’s history for several family members. But everyone knows her favorite hobby was collecting dolls…. LOTS of dolls. Doris loved to travel and camp with friends and family, sharing laughs, building memories, and singing around the campfire. Some of her favorite trips were to Englewood, Florida, Marysville to visit family and road trips to Maine and the Smoky Mountains with her son and daughter-in-law. Doris was preceded in death by her parents, Raymond and Edna; husband, Lawrence “Big Larry”; daughter, Linda; son, Lawrence “Little Larry”; siblings, William, Raymond, Harold, and Richard; son-in-law, Paul Peace; and dear friends, Lillian Dukeshire and Sheila Granata. Doris is survived by her children, Beverly (Paul) Dernier, Kathleen Hendry, Candy Brower, and Douglas (Cathy) Lynch; son-in-law, Michael Newton; brother-in-law, Frank Lynch; sister-in-law, Nancy Stewart; and cousin and dear friend, Martha Rea. Family and friends will be received at the Newcomer Funeral Home (Southwest Chapel) 4752 Heatherdowns Blvd., Toledo on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 from 3:00-8:00PM. Funeral services will be held on Thursday, September 17, 2026 at 11:00 AM. Interment will follow at Ottawa Hills Memorial Park. In lieu of flowers, donations can be made to Elara Caring Hospice.
